Core idea: Cleft sentences ділять інформацію на частини, щоб один елемент отримав особливий emphasis.
Main rule / explanation: It-cleft: It was + focus + who/that... Wh-cleft: What + clause + be + focus. Можна виділити person, thing, time, place, reason.
Form / structure: It was X who/that + clause. What + clause + is/was + focus.
When / why we use it: Використовуй, коли важливо виправити, уточнити або спеціально підкреслити елемент.
Examples:
It was John who called me. → Саме Джон мені зателефонував.
It was the deadline that caused the problem. → Саме дедлайн спричинив проблему.
What I need is more time. → Те, що мені потрібно, — це більше часу.
What she wanted was a clear answer. → Те, чого вона хотіла, — це чітка відповідь.
Special cases / exceptions: Cleft потрібен, коли ми спеціально виділяємо частину інформації: людину, предмет, місце, час або причину.
Common mistakes:
❌ It was John who called me yesterday. (якщо немає причини робити акцент) → ✅ John called me yesterday.
❌ What I need is more time? → ✅ What I need is more time. (це cleft-структура, а не питання.)
Don't confuse with: Запитай: який елемент я хочу виділити? Якщо жоден — звичайне речення може бути кращим.
Quick summary / memory hook:
It-cleft = It was X who/that...
Wh-cleft = What ... is/was X.
Головна функція = emphasis.

Core idea: Relative clauses уточнюють noun. Defining ідентифікує саме яку людину/річ маємо на увазі; non-defining додає додаткову інформацію і використовує commas.
Main rule / explanation: Defining can use who/which/that/where/whose. Non-defining uses who/which/whose, not standard that. Object relative pronoun can sometimes be omitted.
Form / structure: Defining: noun + who/which/that + clause. Non-defining: noun, who/which/whose + clause,.
When / why we use it: Використовуй defining/non-defining relative clauses, щоб ідентифікувати noun або додати додаткову інформацію.
Examples:
The report that you sent is useful. → Звіт, який ти надіслав, корисний.
The report, which you sent yesterday, is useful. → Звіт, який ти надіслав учора, корисний.
The office where I work is nearby. → Офіс, де я працюю, неподалік.
The report (that) I sent was approved. → Звіт, який я надіслав, схвалили.
Special cases / exceptions: Object relative pronoun can be omitted: the report (that) I sent. Subject pronoun normally cannot: the person who called.
Common mistakes:
❌ My manager, that lives nearby,... → ✅ My manager, who lives nearby,...
❌ The person called me. (якщо who = subject relative clause) → ✅ The person who called me.
Don't confuse with: Defining = essential, no commas. Non-defining = extra, commas.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Defining → identifies.
Non-defining → extra information.
that only standard defining.
Object relative can sometimes be omitted.

Core idea: Participle clauses роблять речення коротшими та пов’язують пов’язані дії або описи.
Main rule / explanation: Present participle (-ing) can show simultaneous/related action. Past participle can give passive/background description. Perfect participle having + V3 shows earlier action.
Form / structure: -ing clause. V3 clause. Having + V3 clause.
When / why we use it: Використовуй participle clauses, щоб зробити пов’язані дії або описи коротшими.
Examples:
Walking home, I saw an old friend. → Ідучи додому, я зустрів старого друга.
The people working on the project are experienced. → Люди, які працюють над проєктом, мають досвід.
Built in 1920, the building is still in use. → Будівля, збудована в 1920 році, досі використовується.
Having finished the report, she sent it to the client. → Закінчивши звіт, вона надіслала його клієнту.
Special cases / exceptions: Subject participle clause зазвичай збігається з subject main clause. Інакше виникає dangling participle.
Common mistakes:
❌ Walking down the street, the rain started. → Виходить, ніби дощ ішов вулицею.
✅ Walking down the street, I got caught in the rain.
Don't confuse with: Перевір: хто виконує action у participle clause? Саме цей subject має бути в main clause.
Quick summary / memory hook:
-ing = related/current action.
V3 = passive/background description.
Having + V3 = earlier action.
Avoid dangling participle.

Lesson / Topic: Zero, first, second, and third conditionals
Core idea: Чотири major conditional patterns показують різні відношення між reality та time.
Main rule / explanation: Zero = general truth. First = real future possibility. Second = unreal/unlikely present/future. Third = unreal past. Mixed forms connect different periods.
Form / structure: Zero: If + Present, Present. First: If + Present, will + V1. Second: If + Past, would + V1. Third: If + Past Perfect, would have + V3.
When / why we use it: Використовуй conditional pattern відповідно до поєднання часу та reality.
Examples:
If you heat water to 100°C, it boils. → Якщо нагріти воду до 100°C, вона кипить.
If it rains, we'll stay home. → Якщо піде дощ, ми залишимося вдома.
If I had more time, I would travel more. → Якби в мене було більше часу, я б більше подорожував.
If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train. → Якби ми вийшли раніше, ми б встигли на потяг.
Special cases / exceptions: Choice depends on reality and time, not on the word if itself. Mixed conditionals combine periods.
Common mistakes:
❌ «Є if → завжди Second Conditional». → Ні.
❌ Every hypothetical sentence is Third. → Third is specifically unreal past.
Don't confuse with: Спочатку визнач: general, real future, unreal now/future чи unreal past?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Zero → general truth.
First → realistic future.
Second → unreal now/future.
Third → unreal past.

Core idea: Деякі verbs with two objects можуть утворювати два типи passive sentence, і вибір залежить від того, який object хочемо зробити focus.
Main rule / explanation: Active: They gave me the report / They gave the report to me. Passive: I was given the report / The report was given to me. With tell, personal object often becomes passive subject.
Form / structure: object-person + be + V3 + thing. thing + be + V3 + to + person.
When / why we use it: Використовуй passive, коли person або thing стає головним information focus.
Examples:
They gave me the report. → Вони дали мені звіт.
I was given the report. → Мені дали звіт.
The report was given to me. → Звіт передали мені.
I was told about the change. → Мені повідомили про зміни.
Special cases / exceptions: Не кожен two-object verb однаково природно допускає обидві passive patterns. Учи common constructions.
Common mistakes:
❌ Кожен verb with two objects автоматично має дві однаково природні passive forms. → Ні.
✅ I was told about the change. — природна модель з tell.
Don't confuse with: Запитай: що хочу зробити subject — person чи thing?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Two-object active can have different passive focuses.
I was given the report.
The report was given to me.

Lesson / Topic: Possessive ’s with time expressions – Two hours’ walk
Core idea: Possessive forms with time expressions можуть показувати duration або distance.
Main rule / explanation: Singular time noun: a day's work, one week's notice. Plural time noun ending in s: two weeks' holiday, five years' experience. Expressions can answer «how long?» and describe a distance/time needed.
Form / structure: singular time + 's. plural time ending in s + '.
When / why we use it: Використовуй, коли time expression функціонує як possessive modifier.
Examples:
a day's work. → робота на день.
three weeks' holiday. → тритижнева відпустка.
ten minutes' drive. → десять хвилин їзди.
It's two hours' walk. → Це дві години пішки.
It's a two-hour walk. → Це двогодинна прогулянка.
Special cases / exceptions: Regular plural ending in s takes apostrophe only: hours', weeks', years'. Do not write hours's.
Common mistakes:
❌ two hours's walk → ✅ two hours' walk.
❌ five years's experience → ✅ five years' experience.
Don't confuse with: Compare possessive form and compound adjective: two hours' walk vs a two-hour walk.
Quick summary / memory hook:
singular time → 's.
regular plural time → s'.
No double s'.

Core idea: Compound adjectives об’єднують два або більше слова, які разом описують noun.
Main rule / explanation: Часті patterns: well-known, full-time, user-friendly, high-speed, ten-year-old. Перед noun зазвичай використовується hyphen.
Form / structure: word-word + noun. number + singular noun + adjective ending.
When / why we use it: Використовуй compound adjective як одне визначення перед noun; часто потрібен hyphen.
Examples:
a well-known company. → відома компанія.
a full-time job. → робота на повний день.
a user-friendly interface. → зручний для користувача інтерфейс.
a five-year-old child. → п’ятирічна дитина.
a high-quality product. → високоякісний продукт.
Special cases / exceptions: У number-based compound noun remains singular: five-year-old, not five-years-old. Після noun: The child is five years old.
Common mistakes:
❌ a ten-years project → ✅ a ten-year project.
❌ The child is five-year-old. → ✅ The child is five years old.
Don't confuse with: Перед noun compound acts as one adjective. After noun можна використовувати звичайне plural time expression.
Quick summary / memory hook:
compound adjective before noun → often hyphenated.
number + singular noun.
After noun → normal plural form.

Core idea: Багато nouns мають стійкі поєднання з певними prepositions. У professional English це важливі collocations.
Main rule / explanation: Examples: access to, reason for, solution to, increase in, demand for, effect on, experience in, relationship with, interest in, responsibility for.
Form / structure: noun + preposition + noun/pronoun/V-ing where appropriate.
When / why we use it: Учи noun разом із його typical preposition, а не намагайся перекладати preposition окремо.
Examples:
access to information. → доступ до інформації.
reason for the delay. → причина затримки.
solution to the problem. → рішення проблеми.
increase in prices. → зростання цін.
demand for services. → попит на послуги.
effect on performance. → вплив на performance.
experience in marketing. → досвід у маркетингу.
responsibility for the project. → відповідальність за проєкт.
Special cases / exceptions: Preposition often not predictable from another language. У source emphasis is on memorizing the complete phrase.
Common mistakes: ❌ solution for the problem → ✅ solution to the problem.
Don't confuse with: Не вчи «access» окремо — вчи «access to».
Quick summary / memory hook:
access to.
reason for.
solution to.
increase in.
demand for.
effect on.
experience in.
responsibility for.

Core idea: Comparatives можна посилювати або послаблювати, а також використовувати для опису поступової зміни.
Main rule / explanation: A little/a bit/slightly show small difference. Much/far/a lot show large difference. Even adds emphasis. Comparative + and + comparative shows continuing change. The + comparative, the + comparative shows connected change.
Form / structure: slightly + comparative. much/far/a lot + comparative. even + comparative. comparative and comparative. the + comparative, the + comparative.
When / why we use it: Використовуй, коли важливо не лише порівняти, а й показати розмір difference або process of change.
Examples:
slightly cheaper → трохи дешевший.
a little faster → трохи швидший.
much more expensive → набагато дорожчий.
far better → значно кращий.
a lot easier → набагато легший.
even more useful → ще корисніший.
The situation is getting better and better. → Ситуація стає дедалі кращою.
The more you practise, the easier it becomes. → Чим більше ти практикуєшся, тим легше стає.
Special cases / exceptions: Standard comparative does not combine with very: very better is wrong. Use much better/far better.
Common mistakes:
❌ very better → ✅ much better.
❌ very more expensive → ✅ much more expensive.
Don't confuse with: Спочатку basic comparative, потім modifier, якщо потрібно показати розмір difference.
Quick summary / memory hook:
a bit/slightly = small difference.
much/far/a lot = large difference.
even = extra emphasis.
-er and -er = continuing change.

Lesson / Topic: Reduced infinitives: Omitting the infinitive phrase after 'to'
Core idea: Reduced infinitives дають змогу не повторювати вже зрозумілу частину infinitive phrase.
Main rule / explanation: Після деяких structures можна залишити тільки to. Після modal може залишитися bare verb omission із контекстом: I can help if you want me to. She should have.
Form / structure: want to / promise to etc. → to may remain. modal + understood verb can be omitted.
When / why we use it: Використовуй, коли listener легко відновлює пропущену частину infinitive phrase з контексту.
Examples:
I want to go, but I can't. → Я хочу піти, але не можу.
She didn't call, although she promised to. → Вона не зателефонувала, хоча обіцяла.
I'd like to. → Я б хотів.
He asked me to. → Він попросив мене.
I can help if you want me to. → Я можу допомогти, якщо хочеш, щоб я допоміг.
She didn't finish, although she should have. → Вона не закінчила, хоча мала б.
Special cases / exceptions: Ellipsis/reduced infinitive працює лише при ясному context. Якщо omission створює ambiguity, слова краще повторити.
Common mistakes:
❌ Remove words so listener cannot reconstruct the action. → Тоді скорочення не підходить.
✅ She wants to go, and I want to. → Natural when go is understood.
Don't confuse with: Перевір: чи може listener відновити missing verb phrase без здогадки?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Reduced infinitive = avoid repetition.
After some expressions only to remains.
Modal can leave understood action.
Context is essential.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced present simple and present continuous
Core idea: Вибір Present Simple і Present Continuous на C1 залежить не лише від часу, а й від того, чи йдеться про постійну ситуацію, тимчасову дію, зміну або незвичне повторення.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple частіше показує сталу ситуацію, звичку, факт або стан. Present Continuous показує тимчасову ситуацію, зміну або незвичну/дратівливу повторювану дію.
Form / structure: S + V1/V-s. S + am/is/are + V-ing.
When / why we use it: She works for an international company. = stable fact. She is working from home this month. = temporary. You're always interrupting me. = repeated behaviour viewed as irritating/temporary.
Examples:
She works for an international company. → Вона працює в міжнародній компанії.
She is working from home this month. → Цього місяця вона працює з дому.
More companies are moving their services online. → Все більше компаній переводять свої послуги в онлайн.
You're always interrupting me. → Ти весь час мене перебиваєш.
Special cases / exceptions: Деякі traditionally stative verbs залишаються non-continuous у значенні стану: understand, believe, own. Але окремі verbs змінюють meaning і тоді можуть ставати continuous: I'm having lunch; I'm thinking about the proposal; We are seeing more customers this year.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am understanding the problem. → ✅ I understand the problem.
❌ She owns the company, so she is owning it. → ✅ She owns the company.
Don't confuse with: Не обирай Continuous лише тому, що дія відбувається «зараз». Дивись на meaning: state, activity, temporary situation або developing trend.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Simple → stable/state/repeated.
Continuous → temporary/developing/unusual behaviour.
Meaning matters more than «now».

Lesson / Topic: Advanced past simple, past continuous & past perfect
Core idea: Продвинута робота з past tenses — це організація narrative: що є основною послідовністю, що було фоном, що сталося раніше і що тривало до минулого моменту.
Main rule / explanation: Past Simple = main completed events. Past Continuous = background/in-progress. Past Perfect = earlier past event. Past Perfect Continuous = duration/activity before a past point.
Form / structure: V2. was/were + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: She opened the file, checked the figures and sent the report. / She was checking the figures when the system crashed. / When we arrived, the meeting had already started. / She had been working for hours before she found the cause.
Examples:
She opened the file, checked the figures and sent the report. → Вона відкрила файл, перевірила цифри й надіслала звіт.
She was checking the figures when the system crashed. → Вона перевіряла цифри, коли система вийшла з ладу.
When we arrived, the meeting had already started. → Коли ми прийшли, зустріч уже почалася.
She had been working on the problem for hours before she found the cause. → Вона працювала над проблемою кілька годин, перш ніж знайшла причину.
Special cases / exceptions: Past Perfect не потрібен автоматично для кожної earlier action. Він корисний, коли relationship between past events важливий з обраної narrative viewpoint.
Common mistakes:
❌ Використовувати Past Perfect у кожному реченні про минуле. → Потрібно показати конкретний зв’язок з іншою past point.
❌ She had been work... → ✅ She had been working...
Don't confuse with: Спочатку побудуй timeline. Past Simple = main line; Past Continuous = background; Past Perfect = earlier; Past Perfect Continuous = duration before past point.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Simple = main events.
Past Continuous = background.
Past Perfect = earlier.
Past Perfect Continuous = duration before past point.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced modal verbs: will, would and should
Core idea: Will, would і should можуть виражати не лише майбутнє або пораду. Їхній зміст залежить від ситуації.
Main rule / explanation: Will може показувати готовність, типову поведінку або впевнене припущення. Would може показувати звичку в минулому або пом’якшувати прохання. Should може виражати очікування або те, що вважається нормальним/очікуваним.
Form / structure: will + V1. would + V1. should + V1. Formal conditional: Should + subject + V1...
When / why we use it: I'll help you. → willing. He will often ignore messages. → characteristic behaviour. That will be John calling. → strong expectation. Would you mind checking this? → polite request. The results should be ready by now. → expectation.
Examples:
I'll help you. → Я допоможу тобі.
He will often ignore messages when he's busy. → Він часто ігноруватиме повідомлення, коли зайнятий.
That will be John calling. → Це, мабуть, Джон телефонує.
Would you mind checking this? → Чи не могли б ви це перевірити?
The results should be ready by now. → Результати, за ідеєю, вже мають бути готові.
Should you need assistance, contact the support team. → Якщо вам знадобиться допомога, зверніться до служби підтримки.
Special cases / exceptions: Значення modal залежить від context. Will be at home може бути prediction/strong expectation; would be at home — context-dependent, hypothetical або viewed from past; should be at home — expectation based on what is normally true.
Common mistakes:
❌ Учити will = лише «буду». → На C1 значення залежить від context.
❌ Should always = порада. → Він також може означати expectation або formal conditional.
Don't confuse with: Запитай: speaker is predicting, willing, describing a habit, softening, expecting or giving a formal condition?
Quick summary / memory hook:
will → willingness / typical behaviour / strong expectation.
would → past habit / softer request/opinion.
should → expectation / appropriateness / formal conditional.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced modal verbs: can / be able to, may / might
Core idea: Can і be able to обидва виражають ability, але be able to важливе в інших tenses/aspects і для конкретної успішної події в минулому. May/might виражають possibility.
Main rule / explanation: Can = ability now. Be able to зручно в future/perfect forms. Could = general past ability. Was/were able to або managed to часто ясніше для one specific successful past event. May/might = possibility.
Form / structure: can + V1. be able to + V1. could + V1. may/might + V1. may/might have + V3.
When / why we use it: I can solve the problem. / We'll be able to access the system tomorrow. / We were able to solve the problem. / It may be true. / She might have forgotten.
Examples:
I can solve the problem. → Я можу розв’язати проблему.
We'll be able to access the system tomorrow. → Завтра ми зможемо отримати доступ до системи.
We were able to solve the problem. → Нам вдалося розв’язати проблему.
It may be true. → Можливо, це правда.
She might have forgotten. → Можливо, вона забула.
Special cases / exceptions: Might іноді припускає slightly lower certainty than may, але різниця не завжди сувора. Could не завжди найкращий варіант для one-off successful past event.
Common mistakes:
❌ I'll can access it tomorrow. → ✅ I'll be able to access it tomorrow.
❌ We could solve the specific problem yesterday. → Often clearer: We were able to solve the problem.
Don't confuse with: Can/could — modal. Be able to — flexible tense/aspect. May/might — possibility.
Quick summary / memory hook:
can → ability now.
be able to → flexible tense/aspect.
could → general past ability.
was able to/managed to → specific past success.
may/might → possibility.

Lesson / Topic: The subjunctive in English: Present and past
Core idea: English uses subjunctive-like forms mainly in formal recommendations, demands, necessity and hypothetical structures.
Main rule / explanation: Present subjunctive uses the base form after expressions such as essential, important, insist, demand: It is essential that she be present. British English often also uses should + infinitive. Past subjunctive is most visible in were.
Form / structure: that + subject + V1. Formal BrE: that + subject + should + V1. Hypothetical were: If I were..., I wish it were...
When / why we use it: It is essential that every applicant be informed. / They insisted that he leave immediately. / If I were you, I would wait.
Examples:
It is essential that every applicant be informed. → Дуже важливо, щоб кожного кандидата було поінформовано.
It is important that she be present. → Важливо, щоб вона була присутня.
They insisted that he leave immediately. → Вони наполягали, щоб він негайно пішов.
If I were you, I would wait. → На твоєму місці я б почекав.
I wish it were easier. → Шкода, що це не простіше.
Special cases / exceptions: У British English should + infinitive також поширене після таких виразів. Were у hypothetical structures позначає unreality, а не звичайний past time.
Common mistakes:
❌ It is essential that she is present. → У formal subjunctive pattern: ✅ It is essential that she be present.
❌ If I was you... → Standard formal/hypothetical: ✅ If I were you...
Don't confuse with: Subjunctive form обирається за structure і meaning, а не за звичайною послідовністю часів.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Formal recommendation/demand → base verb.
Hypothetical → were.
Past-looking form may mark unreality, not past time.

Lesson / Topic: The perfect tenses: Forms and uses
Core idea: Perfect forms показують relationship між двома reference points. Perfect — це не просто «минулий час».
Main rule / explanation: Present Perfect links past to now. Present Perfect Continuous emphasizes duration/activity to now. Past Perfect places an event before a past reference point. Past Perfect Continuous emphasizes duration before a past point. Future Perfect and Future Perfect Continuous relate completion/duration to a future reference point.
Form / structure: have/has + V3. have/has been + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing. will have + V3. will have been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Головне питання: щодо якого reference point сталася дія і чи важливі result, activity, duration або completion?
Examples:
I have finished the report. → Я закінчив звіт.
I have been working all morning. → Я працюю весь ранок.
The meeting had started before we arrived. → Зустріч почалася до нашого приходу.
She had been waiting for an hour when he called. → Вона чекала годину, коли він зателефонував.
By Friday, we will have completed the project. → До п’ятниці ми завершимо проєкт.
By June, I will have been working here for ten years. → У червні буде десять років, як я працюватиму тут.
Special cases / exceptions: Perfect is a relationship marker. Не обирай форму лише тому, що дія «в минулому».
Common mistakes:
❌ Перекладати Perfect як окреме слово «вже». → Потрібно дивитися на relationship between reference points.
❌ I had finished when I arrived. → Це змінює timeline: action was completed before arrival.
Don't confuse with: Спочатку вибери reference point. Потім decide: completion/result or activity/duration.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Perfect = relationship between time points.
Simple Perfect → completion/result/experience.
Perfect Continuous → activity/duration.

Core idea: Participle clauses дають змогу стиснути кілька пов’язаних ідей у коротшу formal structure.
Main rule / explanation: Present participle, past participle, perfect participle та perfect passive можуть виражати time, reason, result, condition або accompanying circumstances.
Form / structure: -ing clause. V3 clause. Having + V3. Having been + V3.
When / why we use it: Knowing the risks, they changed the plan. / Designed for small businesses, the system is easy to use. / Having completed the analysis, she presented the results. / Having been informed of the changes, the team adjusted the schedule.
Examples:
Knowing the risks, they changed the plan. → Знаючи про ризики, вони змінили план.
Designed for small businesses, the system is easy to use. → Система, розроблена для малого бізнесу, проста у використанні.
Having completed the analysis, she presented the results. → Завершивши аналіз, вона представила результати.
Having been informed of the changes, the team adjusted the schedule. → Отримавши інформацію про зміни, команда скоригувала графік.
Special cases / exceptions: Implied subject participle clause зазвичай збігається з main clause subject.
Common mistakes:
❌ Having finished the report, the meeting started. → Виходить, ніби meeting завершила звіт.
✅ Having finished the report, I went to the meeting.
Don't confuse with: Перевір: хто виконує дію в participle clause? Цей самий subject має бути в main clause.
Quick summary / memory hook:
-ing = simultaneous/related action.
V3 = passive/background.
Having + V3 = earlier action.
Having been + V3 = earlier passive.

Core idea: Порядок слів можна змінювати, щоб виділити важливу частину повідомлення, протиставити ідеї або поставити довгу інформацію у зручніше місце.
Main rule / explanation: Для виділення information використовуються спеціальні конструкції: іноді частину речення виносять наперед, після negative words змінюють порядок слів, а cleft-constructions прямо показують, що саме важливо.
Form / structure: Normal order. Fronted phrase + clause. Negative adverbial + auxiliary + subject. It-cleft / What-cleft.
When / why we use it: This problem, we need to solve first. / Never have I seen such a result. / Only after the meeting did we understand the problem. / What we need is more time. / It was the deadline that caused the problem.
Examples:
This problem, we need to solve first. → Цю проблему нам потрібно вирішити першою.
Never have I seen such a result. → Я ніколи не бачив такого результату.
Only after the meeting did we understand the problem. → Лише після зустрічі ми зрозуміли проблему.
What we need is more time. → Те, що нам потрібно, — це більше часу.
It was the deadline that caused the problem. → Саме дедлайн спричинив проблему.
Special cases / exceptions: Emphasis often requires a specific syntactic pattern. Просте переміщення слів може створити ungrammatical sentence.
Common mistakes:
❌ Never I have seen... → ✅ Never have I seen...
❌ Only after the meeting we understood... → ✅ Only after the meeting did we understand...
Don't confuse with: Спочатку визнач, яка information має бути prominent, потім обирай структуру, що створює цей focus.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Fronting = emphasis.
Negative/restrictive fronting → inversion.
Cleft = explicit focus.
End-weight = long information later.

Core idea: Prepositions at C1 працюють як частина larger patterns. Їх не можна надійно виводити прямим перекладом.
Main rule / explanation: Prepositions can follow verbs, adjectives and nouns. In questions/relative clauses they can stay at the end or move before whom/which in formal style. Preposition to is followed by -ing.
Form / structure: verb + prep. adjective + prep. noun + prep. preposition + V-ing. Wh + clause + prep.
When / why we use it: depend on, belong to, insist on, object to; responsible for, aware of, capable of, interested in; reason for, solution to, effect on, access to.
Examples:
I depend on the result. → Я залежу від результату.
She is responsible for the project. → Вона відповідає за проєкт.
We need a solution to the problem. → Нам потрібне рішення проблеми.
Who did you speak to? → З ким ти говорив?
To whom did you speak? → З ким ви розмовляли? (formal)
I'm interested in learning. → Я зацікавлений у навчанні.
I look forward to hearing from you. → Чекаю на вашу відповідь.
Special cases / exceptions: To can be a preposition, not infinitive marker: look forward to hearing, object to paying.
Common mistakes:
❌ I look forward to hear from you. → ✅ I look forward to hearing from you.
❌ access of the system → ✅ access to the system.
Don't confuse with: Учи noun/verb/adjective разом із його preposition.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Verb + prep.
Adjective + prep.
Noun + prep.
Preposition to + V-ing.
Formal preposition placement → whom/which.

Core idea: Subject–verb agreement стає складнішим, коли subject відділений від verb, містить quantifiers або є collective noun/amount expression.
Main rule / explanation: Verb agrees with grammatical subject, not the nearest noun. Each/every/everyone take singular verb. Collective nouns can vary by variety and meaning. Amounts/periods can take singular when seen as one unit. Titles usually singular.
Form / structure: singular subject + singular verb. plural subject + plural verb.
When / why we use it: The list of required documents is on the website. / Each employee is responsible. / Everyone has received the message. / Ten minutes is enough. / Five years is a long time.
Examples:
The list of required documents is on the website. → Список необхідних документів знаходиться на сайті.
Each employee is responsible for the result. → Кожен працівник відповідає за результат.
Everyone has received the message. → Усі отримали повідомлення.
Ten minutes is enough. → Десяти хвилин достатньо.
“Great Expectations” is a novel. → «Великі сподівання» — роман.
Special cases / exceptions: Collective nouns can vary: The team is working... / In some British contexts, the team are discussing... Meaning and variety matter.
Common mistakes:
❌ The list of changes are ready. → ✅ The list of changes is ready.
❌ The nearest noun controls the verb. → ✅ Узгодження визначається справжнім subject.
Don't confuse with: Не дивись на nearest noun. Знайди real grammatical subject.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Subject controls agreement.
Don't be distracted by intervening nouns.
each/every/everyone → singular.
Amounts/titles can be singular as units.

Core idea: Above і over обидва можуть означати положення вище, але over частіше пов’язане з покриттям, перетином або рухом через щось.
Main rule / explanation: Above = at a higher level/position. Over = covering/extending across, movement across; over часто використовується і з numbers/quantities.
Form / structure: above + noun. over + noun.
When / why we use it: Обирай за змістом: просто вище → above; покриває/перетинає/рухається через → over.
Examples:
The picture is above the sofa. → Картина над диваном.
The temperature is above zero. → Температура вище нуля.
There is a bridge over the river. → Над річкою є міст.
We flew over the mountains. → Ми летіли над горами.
Over 500 people attended. → Прийшло понад 500 людей.
Special cases / exceptions: У деяких contexts можливі обидва варіанти. Важливий основний relation.
Common mistakes: ❌ Використовувати above автоматично для будь-якого «над». → Якщо важливий crossing/covering, over часто природніше.
Don't confuse with:
above = higher level.
over = covering/crossing/movement; часто > numbers.
Quick summary / memory hook:
above → higher.
over → across/covering/movement.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Although і however обидва виражають contrast, але граматично це різні інструменти.
Main rule / explanation: Although introduces subordinate clause. However is a linking adverb connecting ideas and usually needs punctuation.
Form / structure: although + clause. Sentence. However, sentence.
When / why we use it: Хочемо одну dependent clause → although. Хочемо зв’язати дві самостійні ideas → however.
Examples:
Although it was expensive, we bought it. → Хоча це було дорого, ми це купили.
It was expensive. However, we bought it. → Це було дорого. Однак ми це купили.
The solution is, however, quite expensive. → Рішення, однак, досить дороге.
Special cases / exceptions: У standard concise usage не став however безпосередньо після although.
Common mistakes:
❌ Although it was expensive, however, we bought it. → ✅ Although it was expensive, we bought it.
❌ However it was expensive, we bought it. → ✅ Although it was expensive, we bought it.
Don't confuse with: although = grammar connector inside one structure. however = linking adverb.
Quick summary / memory hook:
although + clause.
however + separate idea/punctuation.

Lesson / Topic: Amount of vs Number of vs Quantity of
Core idea: Number of, amount of і quantity of обираються за типом noun та значенням quantity.
Main rule / explanation: Number of → plural countable nouns. Amount of → uncountable nouns. Quantity of → countable or uncountable, especially measurable quantity.
Form / structure: the/a large number of + plural noun. the/a large amount of + uncountable. the/a large quantity of + countable/uncountable.
When / why we use it: Countable employees/questions → number. Uncountable money/information/traffic → amount. Measurable quantity → quantity.
Examples:
The number of employees has increased. → Кількість працівників зросла.
The amount of traffic has increased. → Обсяг трафіку зріс.
A large quantity of water was needed. → Потрібна була велика кількість води.
Special cases / exceptions: Quantity of може вживатися і з countable, і з uncountable; вона підкреслює measurable quantity.
Common mistakes:
❌ the amount of employees → ✅ the number of employees.
❌ a number of money → ✅ an amount of money.
Don't confuse with: Спочатку визнач: countable or uncountable?
Quick summary / memory hook:
number → plural countable.
amount → uncountable.
quantity → both, measurable.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: How to avoid double subjects in English
Core idea: У стандартній англійській clause зазвичай має один grammatical subject. Не додавай pronoun після noun, який уже є subject.
Main rule / explanation: Normal: The manager approved the request. Нейтрально не потрібно: The manager, he approved... У relative clause також не можна додавати зайвий subject.
Form / structure: one grammatical subject per clause. Relative clause keeps its own subject/object structure.
When / why we use it: Спочатку знайди subject і перевір, чи не повторюєш його другим pronoun.
Examples:
The manager approved the request. → Менеджер затвердив запит.
The report that I sent yesterday is ready. → Звіт, який я надіслав учора, готовий.
Тут that — додаток до sent, а не зайвий підмет.
Special cases / exceptions: У розмовній мові можливий marked pattern My brother, he works in IT., але це не neutral standard structure.
Common mistakes:
❌ The manager, he approved the request. → ✅ The manager approved the request.
❌ The report that I sent it yesterday... → ✅ The report that I sent yesterday...
Don't confuse with: Не додавай pronoun, якщо noun уже виконує роль subject/object у структурі.
Quick summary / memory hook:
One clause → one normal subject.
Avoid repeated subject pronouns.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Between і among пов’язані з положенням/відносинами всередині групи, але важливий не лише count предметів.
Main rule / explanation: Between traditionally пов’язане з two, але може вживатися з more than two, коли розглядаються individual relationships. Among = всередині групи/розподіл.
Form / structure: between + people/things. among + group.
When / why we use it: Use between when individual items/relationships are in focus. Among when inside a group or distributed within it.
Examples:
The agreement is between the two companies. → Угода між двома компаніями.
The negotiations between the five countries continued. → Переговори між п’ятьма країнами тривали.
She was sitting among her colleagues. → Вона сиділа серед колег.
The money was divided among the participants. → Гроші розділили між учасниками/серед учасників.
Special cases / exceptions: Не вчи просте правило «between = 2, among = 3+» як absolute.
Common mistakes: ❌ Between can only be used with two. → Ні: between five countries possible when individual relationships are considered.
Don't confuse with: Дивись: individual relationships або group context?
Quick summary / memory hook:
between → individual relationships/items.
among → within a group/distribution.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Bring і take обираються за viewpoint: рух до speaker/reference point або від нього.
Main rule / explanation: Bring = movement toward the speaker or place being discussed. Take = movement away from speaker/current location.
Form / structure: bring + object + to destination. take + object + to destination.
When / why we use it: Уяви точку зору мовця: куди рухається object відносно цієї reference point?
Examples:
Bring your laptop to the meeting. → Принеси ноутбук на зустріч.
Take these documents to the manager. → Віднеси ці документи менеджеру.
Can you bring the report to my office? → Можеш принести звіт до мого офісу?
Can you take this report to Sarah? → Можеш віднести цей звіт Сарі?
Special cases / exceptions: Головне — viewpoint, а не просто фізичний напрямок предмета.
Common mistakes: ❌ Обирати bring/take лише за рухом предмета. → Дивись, де speaker/reference point.
Don't confuse with:
bring → toward reference point.
take → away from reference point.
Quick summary / memory hook: Viewpoint decides bring vs take.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Clean і wash обидва можуть стосуватися видалення бруду, але focus різний.
Main rule / explanation: Clean = зробити чистим, прибрати бруд/пил/небажаний матеріал. Wash = використовувати water/liquid у процесі cleaning.
Form / structure: clean + object. wash + object.
When / why we use it: Коли важливий загальний результат «очистити» → clean. Коли важливий water/liquid → wash.
Examples:
Clean the kitchen. → Прибери/почисть кухню.
I cleaned my shoes. → Я почистив взуття.
Wash your hands. → Вимий руки.
I washed the car. → Я помив машину.
The equipment must be cleaned regularly. → Обладнання потрібно регулярно очищати.
Special cases / exceptions: Деякі objects можуть мати both clean and wash: clean the windows = remove dirt; wash the windows = use water.
Common mistakes:
❌ Wash the kitchen. (якщо загальний процес прибирання) → ✅ Clean the kitchen.
❌ Clean your hands. → У звичайній everyday usage: Wash your hands.
Don't confuse with: clean = remove dirt / make clean. wash = clean using water/liquid.
Quick summary / memory hook:
clean = general cleaning.
wash = with water/liquid.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Come і go залежать від reference point: рух до speaker/listener/shared destination або від reference point.
Main rule / explanation: Come = movement toward speaker or another shared reference point. Go = movement away from that point.
Form / structure: come + destination. go + destination.
When / why we use it: Дивись на viewpoint speaker/listener/shared destination.
Examples:
Come here. → Іди сюди.
Are you coming to the meeting? → Ти прийдеш на зустріч?
I'm going home. → Я йду/їду додому.
She went to the office. → Вона пішла в офіс.
Special cases / exceptions: Reference point може бути shared destination, навіть якщо speaker ще не знаходиться там.
Common mistakes: ❌ Обирати come/go лише за тим, чи speaker уже на місці. → Shared destination can be reference point.
Don't confuse with:
come → toward reference point.
go → away from reference point.
Quick summary / memory hook: Reference point decides come vs go.

Core idea: Have been to і have gone to відрізняються тим, чи повернулася людина з місця до reference time.
Main rule / explanation: Have been to = visited and returned. Have gone to = went there and is still away / not returned at reference time.
Form / structure: have/has been to + place. have/has gone to + place.
When / why we use it: Для life experience → been to. Для current absence/presence elsewhere → gone to.
Examples:
I've been to London twice. → Я двічі був у Лондоні.
Sarah has gone to the supermarket. → Сара пішла до супермаркету.
Tom has been to Spain. → Том був в Іспанії.
Tom has gone to Spain. → Том поїхав до Іспанії й ще не повернувся.
Special cases / exceptions: Context decides whether person has returned.
Common mistakes: ❌ I've gone to London twice. (якщо йдеться про past experience and return) → ✅ I've been to London twice.
Don't confuse with:
been to = visited and returned.
gone to = went and is still away.

Experience → been.
Currently away → gone.

Core idea: If і whether обидва можуть вводити indirect yes/no question, але whether має додаткові grammatical uses.
Main rule / explanation: If/whether both possible in many indirect questions. Whether is preferred/more formal in some contexts and required before infinitive, with or not, and after a preposition.
Form / structure: if/whether + clause. whether + to + V1. whether or not + clause. prep + whether + clause.
When / why we use it: Дивись на position: simple indirect question часто допускає both; special constructions → whether.
Examples:
I don't know if she is coming. → Я не знаю, чи вона прийде.
I don't know whether she is coming. → Я не знаю, чи вона прийде.
We need to decide whether to stay. → Нам потрібно вирішити, чи залишатися.
I don't know whether or not he agrees. → Я не знаю, чи згоден він чи ні.
It depends on whether they accept. → Це залежить від того, чи вони погодяться.
Special cases / exceptions: Whether особливо зручно перед to + V1, після preposition і в конструкції whether or not.
Common mistakes:
❌ decide if to stay → ✅ decide whether to stay.
❌ It depends on if they accept. → ✅ It depends on whether they accept.
Don't confuse with: В ordinary indirect yes/no question обидва можуть працювати. У special positions → whether.
Quick summary / memory hook:
if/whether = indirect yes/no question.
whether + to V1.
whether or not.
preposition + whether.

Core idea: Instead і instead of обидва показують alternative, але граматично працюють по-різному.
Main rule / explanation: Instead = adverb. Instead of = preposition і після нього йде noun, pronoun або V-ing.
Form / structure: instead. instead of + noun/pronoun/V-ing.
When / why we use it: Instead часто замінює whole alternative: We didn't take the train. We drove instead. Instead of вводить action/object, який замінюємо.
Examples:
We didn't take the train. We drove instead. → Ми не поїхали потягом. Натомість ми поїхали машиною.
Instead, we decided to walk. → Натомість ми вирішили піти пішки.
We walked instead of taking the bus. → Ми пішли пішки замість автобуса.
She called instead of sending an email. → Вона зателефонувала замість того, щоб надсилати email.
Special cases / exceptions: Після instead of, якщо далі verb, використовуємо -ing.
Common mistakes:
❌ instead of wait → ✅ instead of waiting.
❌ We drove instead of the train. → Better meaning depends on intended structure: We drove instead.
Don't confuse with: adverb vs preposition.
Quick summary / memory hook:
instead = as an alternative.
instead of + noun/pronoun/V-ing.

Core idea: Its і it's відрізняються так само чітко, як possessive і contraction.
Main rule / explanation: Its = possessive determiner. It's = it is or it has.
Form / structure: its + noun. it's = it is / it has.

Examples:
The company changed its policy. → Компанія змінила свою політику.
It's cold today. → Сьогодні холодно.
It's been a long day. → День був довгим.
Special cases / exceptions: Possessive its does not take apostrophe.
Common mistakes:
❌ The company changed it's policy. → ✅ The company changed its policy.
❌ Its cold today. → ✅ It's cold today.
Don't confuse with: Possession → its. Contraction → it's.

its = possessive.
it's = it is / it has.

Lesson / Topic: Last vs The last, Next vs The next
Core idea: Last і next змінюють значення залежно від наявності the. Без the вони часто стосуються періоду відносно now; з the — конкретного елемента в sequence.
Main rule / explanation: Last week = week immediately before this one. The last week of the course = final week of that course. Next week = following week from now. The next week = following week in a sequence/narrative.
Form / structure: last/next + time period. the last/the next + noun in a sequence.
When / why we use it: Дивись, чи говоримо ми про calendar period relative to now, чи про item у specific sequence.
Examples:
I saw her last week. → Я бачив її минулого тижня.
The last week of the course was difficult. → Останній тиждень курсу був складним.
I'll see you next week. → Побачимося наступного тижня.
The next week was much quieter. → Наступний тиждень був набагато спокійнішим.
Special cases / exceptions: Article changes the meaning depending on context.
Common mistakes: ❌ Treat next month and the next month as always identical. → Context distinguishes them.
Don't confuse with:
last/next = relation to now often.
the last/the next = item in a sequence/context.
Quick summary / memory hook: Article changes the reference point.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Lie і lay відрізняються тим, чи є дієслово intransitive «лежати», чи transitive «класти щось».
Main rule / explanation: Lie = be in a horizontal position: lie–lay–lain. Lay = put something somewhere: lay–laid–laid.
Form / structure: lie + no direct object. lay + direct object.
When / why we use it: Дивись, чи є object: I lie down. / I lay the book down.
Examples:
I need to lie down. → Мені потрібно лягти.
She is lying on the bed. → Вона лежить на ліжку.
Please lay the book on the table. → Поклади книгу на стіл.
He laid the keys on the desk. → Він поклав ключі на стіл.
Special cases / exceptions: Past of lie (recline) is lay. Lay має власний past laid. Саме це часто спричиняє confusion.
Common mistakes:
❌ Yesterday I laid on the sofa. → ✅ Yesterday I lay on the sofa.
❌ He lay the keys on the desk. → ✅ He laid the keys on the desk.
Don't confuse with: lie = position/state. lay = put something.
Quick summary / memory hook:
lie – lay – lain.
lay – laid – laid.
Object after lay.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Fewer зазвичай вживається з plural countable nouns, less — з uncountable nouns.
Main rule / explanation: fewer mistakes/employees/problems. less time/money/information. In measurement expressions less can be natural: less than ten minutes.
Form / structure: fewer + plural countable. less + uncountable.
When / why we use it: Спочатку визнач grammatical type noun.
Examples:
We need fewer meetings. → Нам потрібно менше нарад.
We need less paperwork. → Нам потрібно менше паперової роботи.
It took less than ten minutes. → Це зайняло менше десяти хвилин.
Special cases / exceptions: У measurement expressions less common: less than five kilometres. Не обирай лише за тим, що в українській це «окремі речі».
Common mistakes:
❌ less employees → ✅ fewer employees.
❌ fewer information → ✅ less information.
Don't confuse with:
countable plural → fewer.
uncountable → less.
Quick summary / memory hook:
fewer = countable plural.
less = uncountable.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Like і as можуть перекладатися подібно, але like зазвичай порівнює, а as вводить clause або показує role/function.
Main rule / explanation: Like is usually preposition before noun/pronoun. As can introduce a clause or describe a role/function.
Form / structure: like + noun/pronoun. as + clause. as + role/noun.
When / why we use it: Запитай: «схожий на?» → like. «у ролі/так, як» → as.
Examples:
She works like a professional. → Вона працює як професіонал (схоже на професіонала).
It looks like rain. → Схоже на дощ.
Do it as I showed you. → Зроби так, як я тобі показав.
He works as a designer. → Він працює дизайнером.
As you know, the meeting starts at nine. → Як ти знаєш, зустріч починається о дев’ятій.
Special cases / exceptions: У більш формальному мовленні as зазвичай використовується перед повноцінною частиною речення: Do it as I told you.
Common mistakes:
❌ He works like a designer. (якщо це actual role) → ✅ He works as a designer.
❌ Do it like I told you. → Standard formal: ✅ Do it as I told you.
Don't confuse with:
like = resemblance.
as = role/function or clause.
Quick summary / memory hook:
like + noun/pronoun.
as + clause/role.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Little vs A little, Few vs A few
Core idea: Little/few без a часто передають значення «мало, майже недостатньо». A little/a few показують невеликий, але реальний amount/number.
Main rule / explanation: Little + uncountable. A little + uncountable. Few + plural countable. A few + plural countable.
Form / structure: little/a little + uncountable. few/a few + plural countable.
When / why we use it: Головна різниця — article a змінює відтінок: almost none/insufficient vs some amount/number.
Examples:
We have little time. → У нас мало часу, ймовірно, недостатньо.
We have a little time. → У нас є трохи часу.
Few people understood the problem. → Мало хто зрозумів проблему.
A few people understood the problem. → Кілька людей зрозуміли проблему.
Special cases / exceptions: Article a changes meaning significantly. Порівняй little hope vs a little hope.
Common mistakes:
❌ a little people → ✅ a few people.
❌ a few time → ✅ a little time.
Don't confuse with:
little/a little → uncountable.
few/a few → plural countable.
a = small but real amount/number.
Quick summary / memory hook:
a little/a few = some.
little/few = not much/not many.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: See, look і watch описують різні види visual perception.
Main rule / explanation: See = perception without deliberate effort. Look = direct your eyes toward something and normally needs at + object. Watch = observe for a period, especially something moving/changing.
Form / structure: see + object. look at + object. watch + object.
When / why we use it: Запитай: просто помітити → see. Спрямувати погляд → look at. Спостерігати певний час → watch.
Examples:
I can see the mountains. → Я бачу гори.
Look at this picture. → Подивися на цю картинку.
We watched a film. → Ми подивилися фільм.
She watched the children playing. → Вона спостерігала, як діти граються.
Special cases / exceptions: Look needs at у basic pattern, коли означає direct your eyes toward something.
Common mistakes:
❌ Look the screen. → ✅ Look at the screen.
❌ I watched the mountains from the window. → Usually: I saw the mountains / looked at the mountains, depending on intended meaning.
Don't confuse with:
see = perception.
look at = directed attention.
watch = sustained observation.
Quick summary / memory hook:
see = notice.
look at = direct eyes.
watch = observe over time.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Maybe і may be звучать однаково, але це різні граматичні конструкції.
Main rule / explanation: Maybe = adverb meaning perhaps. May be = modal may + verb be.
Form / structure: Maybe + clause. subject + may be + complement.
When / why we use it: Якщо можна замінити на perhaps → maybe. Якщо modal + be є частиною verb phrase → may be.
Examples:
Maybe she is busy. → Можливо, вона зайнята.
She may be busy. → Можливо, вона зайнята.
Maybe we'll go tomorrow. → Може бути, ми поїдемо завтра.
They may be late. → Можливо, вони запізняться.
Special cases / exceptions: Position reveals structure: Maybe often stands at sentence level; may be is part of predicate.
Common mistakes:
❌ She maybe busy. → ✅ She may be busy. / Maybe she is busy.
❌ Maybe she may be busy. → Possible but changes emphasis; don't use one as a spelling variant of the other.
Don't confuse with:
maybe = perhaps.
may be = modal + be.
Quick summary / memory hook:
maybe = one word adverb.
may be = two-word verb phrase.

Core idea: Never і ever обидва пов’язані з time/frequency, але працюють по-різному.
Main rule / explanation: Never = at no time. Ever is common in questions, conditionals and superlative-like expressions.
Form / structure: never + verb. Have you ever...? if you ever... best ... I've ever...
When / why we use it: Ever часто використовується, коли запитуємо «коли-небудь?» або говоримо «коли-небудь/будь-коли». Never уже містить negative meaning.
Examples:
I've never been there. → Я ніколи там не був.
She never complains. → Вона ніколи не скаржиться.
Have you ever been to Spain? → Ти коли-небудь був в Іспанії?
If you ever need help, call me. → Якщо тобі коли-небудь знадобиться допомога, зателефонуй мені.
This is the best result I've ever seen. → Це найкращий результат, який я коли-небудь бачив.
Special cases / exceptions: У standalone affirmative statement ever зазвичай не замінює never.
Common mistakes: ❌ I've ever seen it. → ✅ I've never seen it. / This is the best I've ever seen.
Don't confuse with:
never = no time.
ever = questions/conditions/experience/emphasis.
Quick summary / memory hook:
never = at no time.
ever = at any time, commonly in questions/conditions.

Lesson / Topic: On the other hand vs On the contrary
Core idea: On the other hand і on the contrary обидва можуть зв’язувати ideas, але виражають різні відношення.
Main rule / explanation: On the other hand introduces another side/aspect of an issue. On the contrary directly contradicts or corrects a previous statement/assumption.
Form / structure: Sentence. On the other hand, sentence. / On the contrary, sentence.
When / why we use it: Використовуй on the other hand, коли показуєш іншу сторону; on the contrary — коли кажеш «навпаки, це не так».
Examples:
The job is well paid. On the other hand, the hours are long. → Робота добре оплачується. З іншого боку, робочий день довгий.
“I thought the task was difficult.” “On the contrary, it was quite easy.” → «Я думав, що завдання складне». «Навпаки, воно було досить легким».
Special cases / exceptions: On the contrary requires direct contradiction/correction, not merely different information.
Common mistakes:
❌ Two different facts = automatically on the contrary. → Ні; often on the other hand.
✅ On the contrary, it was easy. → direct correction.
Don't confuse with:
other hand = another aspect.
contrary = opposite of what was suggested.
Quick summary / memory hook:
on the other hand = інший аспект.
on the contrary = пряме спростування.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Raise і rise відрізняються transitivity: raise зазвичай потребує object, rise — зазвичай ні.
Main rule / explanation: Raise = someone raises something. Rise = something rises by itself. Forms: raise–raised–raised; rise–rose–risen.
Form / structure: raise + object. rise + subject/no direct object.
When / why we use it: Запитай: хтось піднімає/збільшує щось? → raise. Щось саме підвищується/піднімається? → rise.
Examples:
They raised the price. → Вони підвищили ціну.
She raised her hand. → Вона підняла руку.
Prices rise. → Ціни зростають.
The sun rises. → Сонце сходить.
The temperature is rising. → Температура підвищується.
Special cases / exceptions: Rise is intransitive in this basic distinction. Raise takes a direct object.
Common mistakes:
❌ They rose the price. → ✅ They raised the price.
❌ She raised. → Needs object in this meaning: She raised her hand.
Don't confuse with:
raise = transitive.
rise = intransitive.
Quick summary / memory hook:
raise–raised–raised.
rise–rose–risen.
Object → raise.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Remember & Forget: To Do vs Doing
Core idea: Remember/forget + to V1 стосуються дії, яку потрібно/потрібно було виконати. + V-ing — memory of an action that happened.
Main rule / explanation: to-infinitive = task/action to do. V-ing = memory/experience of doing.
Form / structure: remember/forget + to + V1. remember/forget + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Порівняй: Did I remember the task? vs Do I remember the event?
Examples:
Remember to send the email. → Не забудь надіслати email.
I forgot to call him. → Я забув йому зателефонувати.
I remember meeting her. → Я пам’ятаю, як із нею познайомився.
I'll never forget visiting that place. → Я ніколи не забуду, що побував у тому місці.
I remembered to lock the door. → Я не забув замкнути двері.
I remember locking the door. → Я пам’ятаю, як замкнув двері.
Special cases / exceptions: Різниця не просто в часі. Вона в relationship between remembering and the action.
Common mistakes:
❌ I forgot meeting her. = «я забув, що мав із нею зустрітися». → ✅ I forgot to meet her. (забув зробити).
❌ I remembered meeting her. = «я згадав, що мав із нею зустрітися». → ✅ I remember meeting her. (пам’ятаю подію зустрічі).
Don't confuse with:
to do = remember/forget the task.
doing = memory of past action.
Quick summary / memory hook:
remember/forget + to do → task.
remember/forget + doing → memory.

Core idea: Say і tell обидва передають інформацію, але tell зазвичай потребує object — людини, якій щось повідомляють.
Main rule / explanation: Say focuses on words/message. Tell focuses on communicating to someone and usually takes an object in this reporting pattern.
Form / structure:
say something / say that...
tell someone something / tell someone to do something
tell the truth / tell a story / tell a joke / tell the time
When / why we use it: Спочатку визнач, чи названий receiver of message.
Examples:
She said that she was tired. → Вона сказала, що втомилася.
She told me that she was tired. → Вона сказала мені, що втомилася.
He told us the truth. → Він сказав нам правду.
He told a joke. → Він розповів жарт.
Tell me the time, please. → Скажи мені, котра година.
Special cases / exceptions: Після tell часто називають отримувача, але не завжди. Стійкі сполучення tell the truth, tell a lie, tell a story, tell a joke, tell the time вживаються без нього.
Common mistakes:
❌ He said me the truth. → ✅ He told me the truth.
❌ He told me to the truth. → ✅ He told me the truth.
❌ She told that she was tired. → ✅ She said that she was tired. / She told me that she was tired.
❌ He said a joke. → ✅ He told a joke.
Don't confuse with:
say = words/message.
tell = tell someone.
Quick summary / memory hook:
say something.
say that...
tell someone something.
tell someone to do.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Try to do vs Try doing
Core idea: Try to do і try doing обидва можуть перекладатися як «спробувати», але focus різний.
Main rule / explanation: Try to do = make an effort to perform an action. Try doing = experiment with an action/method to see whether it works.
Form / structure: try + to + V1. try + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Запитай: йдеться про спробу виконати action чи про experiment із можливим solution?
Examples:
Try to restart the computer. → Спробуй перезапустити комп’ютер.
I tried to contact the client. → Я намагався зв’язатися з клієнтом.
Try restarting the computer. → Спробуй перезапустити комп’ютер (як спосіб вирішення).
Try using a different browser. → Спробуй інший браузер.
Special cases / exceptions: Це не просто two stylistic alternatives. Infinitive focuses on effort; -ing often suggests method/experiment.
Common mistakes:
❌ Try to restarting the computer. → ✅ Try restarting the computer.
❌ Try doing to contact the client. → ✅ Try to contact the client.
Don't confuse with:
to do = effort.
doing = experiment/method.
Quick summary / memory hook:
try to do = make an effort.
try doing = test a method.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Until і by відповідають на різні питання про час: дія тривала до моменту або має завершитися не пізніше deadline.
Main rule / explanation: Until = situation/action continues up to a time. By = deadline/latest time something will happen.
Form / structure: verb + until + time. verb + by + time.
When / why we use it: Для continuous duration → until. Для deadline/completion → by.
Examples:
I'll work until six. → Я працюватиму до шостої.
She stayed there until Friday. → Вона залишалася там до п’ятниці.
Please finish it by six. → Закінчи це до шостої.
I'll have sent the report by Friday. → До п’ятниці я вже надішлю звіт.
Special cases / exceptions: Until can mean «не раніше», depending on context: Send it until Friday is not a normal way to express a deadline.
Common mistakes:
❌ Please finish it until six. → ✅ Please finish it by six.
✅ I won't send it until Friday. → Тут until means «не раніше п’ятниці».
Don't confuse with:
until = continuation up to a time.
by = deadline/latest time.
Quick summary / memory hook:
until → continues to.
by → completed no later than.
QA / notes: Translated directly from the RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Whereas і while обидва можуть порівнювати дві ситуації, але while має додаткові meanings.
Main rule / explanation: Whereas mainly contrasts facts/characteristics. While can contrast, express time, or sometimes concession.
Form / structure: whereas + clause. while + clause.
When / why we use it: Якщо потрібен лише contrast between facts → whereas. Якщо while — determine from context whether it means time or contrast.
Examples:

Core idea: Wish, hope і expect пов’язані з future/desired situations, але виражають різне ставлення до reality.
Main rule / explanation: Hope = desired and realistically possible. Expect = believe something is likely/anticipated. Wish = unreal, unlikely or impossible situation, or regret.
Form / structure: hope + clause/to V1. expect + noun/to V1/that-clause. wish + unreal structure.
When / why we use it: Використовуй, щоб розрізняти realistic desire, expectation і unreal/regret.
Examples:
I hope we can finish today. → Я сподіваюся, що ми зможемо закінчити сьогодні.
I expect the meeting to finish at five. → Я очікую, що зустріч закінчиться о п’ятій.
I wish I had more time. → Шкода, що в мене немає більше часу.
I wish you were here. → Шкода, що тебе тут немає.
We wish you a pleasant journey. → Бажаємо вам приємної подорожі.
Special cases / exceptions: Wish is not a simple synonym for hope when the desired event is realistically possible.
Common mistakes:
❌ I wish we can finish today. → For realistic possibility: ✅ I hope we can finish today.
❌ I expect I had more time. → For unreal present: ✅ I wish I had more time.
Don't confuse with: Спроси: realistic desire → hope; likely expectation → expect; unreal/regret → wish.
Quick summary / memory hook:
hope = desired + possible.
expect = likely/anticipated.
wish = unreal/regret.
